idea: Basic plumbing maintenance every homeowner should know
title: Understanding and Maintaining the P-Trap Water Seal
description: The P-trap beneath your sink does more than catch lost rings—its primary job is holding a standing pocket of water that seals out sewer gases. When a fixture goes unused for weeks, this water seal evaporates, allowing foul odors into your living space. Additionally, slow drains are often caused by hair and debris trapped right in this curved section. Before reaching for aggressive chemical drain cleaners, place a small bucket beneath the trap and unscrew the slip nuts by hand to clean it mechanically. What plumbing maintenance task do you check first when a sink starts to smell?

visual_story: The visual uses a clear sectional cutaway of a white plastic under-sink P-trap to show the standing water level inside the curve. Viewers can immediately see how the retained water forms a liquid plug between the household side and the main drainage network. The clear geometry highlights the slip-nut joints, making it easy to understand where the trap can be disconnected for routine cleaning.

on_image_text.hook: Why Your Sink Smell Isn't Always a Main Clog
on_image_text.explanation: A standing water seal inside the P-trap blocks sewer gas from rising up your drain line.
on_image_text.takeaway: Run unused sinks regularly to keep the seal full, or clear clogs mechanically by removing the slip nuts.
